title: Cancer Breakthroughs Update — May 15, 2026
summary: The FDA approved sonrotoclax (Beqalzi) on May 13 as the first BCL-2 inhibitor specifically targeting relapsed/refractory mantle cell lymphoma after BTK inhibitor failure, with 52% overall response rate and 15.8-month median duration of response in 103 patients — addressing a critical unmet need in BTK-resistant MCL. On May 8, Bizengri (zenocutuzumab) received accelerated approval for NRG1 fusion-positive bile duct cancer, extending the bispecific HER2/HER3 antibody's pan-tumor reach to three NRG1+ cancer types. The FDA also granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to emiltatug ledadotin (ADC) for adenoid cystic carcinoma on May 12 — one of the most promising early targeted therapy candidates for this rare, incurable salivary gland malignancy. Additionally, the liquid biopsy field's resolution section has been updated to reflect the February 2026 NHS-Galleri trial miss (primary endpoint not met), adding context for the ongoing debate over MCED screening readiness. ASCO 2026 full abstracts release on May 21, with daraxonrasib's Phase 3 plenary on May 31.

title: Cancer Breakthroughs Update — May 07, 2026
summary: The world's first PROTAC protein degrader drug, Veppanu (vepdegestrant), received FDA approval on May 1 for ESR1-mutant ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer — inaugurating a new therapeutic class that destroys the estrogen receptor rather than blocking it. The FDA simultaneously authorized expanded access for daraxonrasib in pancreatic cancer following Phase 3 data showing 13.2 vs. 6.7 months median OS. Daraxonrasib's Phase 1/2 results were published in NEJM on May 6 (30% response rate at 300 mg). Additional developments include a JACR study showing AI mammography triage captures 50% of screen-detected cancers in the top 2% of scans, and a Mount Sinai Cell Reports Medicine paper demonstrating that quad-target immunotherapy (PD-1+CTLA-4+LAG-3+TREM2) overcomes checkpoint resistance in treatment-refractory colorectal cancer.

title: Cancer Breakthroughs Update — Apr 30, 2026
summary: AACR 2026 follow-up delivered multiple landmark results this week. CAR-PRISM Phase 2 showed Carvykti achieving 100% MRD negativity in all 20 smoldering myeloma patients. NEOPRISM-CRC reported zero relapses at 33 months with pembrolizumab-only pre-surgery approach for MSI-high bowel cancer. ASCENT-04/KEYNOTE-D19 (NEJM) demonstrated Trodelvy + Keytruda outperforming chemo + immunotherapy in first-line PD-L1+ advanced TNBC (PFS 11.2 vs 7.8 months). Additional developments include MK-2010 bispecific (55% ORR in NSCLC), FDA Priority Review for PADCEV + Keytruda in perioperative bladder cancer, and today's FDA AdCom review of camizestrant for ESR1-mutant breast cancer.
